texts: the path starts by the pond
the path goes up the hill
the shell has a small opening
the snail slides on its foot
the snail pulls its head in
the snail pulls its foot in
the shell covers its soft body
a chick grows inside one egg
the chick pushes its way out
this chick grows into a hen
kit has red and blue tiles
each color has its own group
each shape has its own group
the same tiles can change groups
her old box is a bed
i want to close my own bag
i push. the button will not go through
i turn the button on its edge
i slide one edge through the hole
i pull the button the rest of the way
one is done. i try the next
the last one is tricky. i try again
three buttons done. i did them myself
zoe taps her drum. kit has a drum too
"listen to my beat," says zoe. tap, tap, tap
kit bangs his drum. he cannot hear zoe
zoe stops. her hands rest on her knees
kit stops too. "play it again," he says
zoe taps. kit listens with still hands
now kit taps the same beat. zoe listens
kit stops. he nods. zoe taps an answer
zoe wants to borrow kit's fox book
"this book goes back today," says kit
"let's return it. then you can borrow it."
kit puts the book on the returns desk
the worker checks the book back in
zoe shows her card. she borrows the book
zoe opens the book. kit sits beside her
they find the fox. now zoe turns the page
one clap makes the red boot hop
kit wants the boot in its box
kit grabs. the boot slips from his hands
kit claps again. the boot hops farther away
he puts the box in the boot's path
one clap. the boot hops into the box
kit puts the lid on the box
kit waves. the box stays still
this small stream runs down a hill
its water slips around the rocks
the stream flows into a wide river
the river carries the water through the valley
the river grows wide near the sea
fresh river water meets salty sea water
from hill to river to sea. one connected path
a boot presses into the moon's gray dust
the boot lifts. a deep print stays
more steps make a trail of boot prints
on earth, rain can wash prints away
no rain falls on the moon
no wind blows the moon dust around
the boot prints can stay for a long time
the boots are gone. their marks are still here
a duck swims across the pond
her feet move under the water
skin joins the toes on each wide foot
her wide foot pushes back against the water
the duck moves forward. her feet keep paddling
she reaches the bank and steps out
wide feet for water. feet for land too
tiny yellow eggs cling to a leaf
a young ladybug hatches. it is a larva
the larva eats tiny green bugs
it grows. its tight skin comes off
it stays still. its body changes inside
the grown ladybug comes out looking pale
its body hardens. dark spots show
this ladybug lays eggs on a leaf
zoe spreads six buttons on the mat
she puts the red buttons together
she puts the blue buttons together
two color groups. big and small are mixed
zoe tips all the buttons back out
this time, she puts the big buttons together
the small buttons go in the other group
same buttons. new groups. zoe sorts by size
kit puts three blocks in his cloth bag
one block falls through a hole
kit puts it back and folds the corner. the block falls again
kit empties the bag. zoe finds a patch and asks for help
the grown-up sews. kit holds the bag still
the blue patch covers the hole
kit puts the same three blocks back inside
he lifts the bag. all three blocks stay in
kit wants to put on a puppet show. he builds a little stage from blocks
he draws a dog for the show. its legs look more like sticks
zoe has drawn a dog with floppy ears. her paper stage keeps falling flat
kit studies her folded paper. "it needs something stiff behind it."
he props the paper against his block stage. this time it stays up
zoe adds a red collar to her dog. "would you like to use this?"
kit moves the dog above the stage. zoe makes it bark from the side
"woof!" the paper dog takes a bow. kit laughs, and zoe barks again
zoe sets a hoop on the grass. "throw your ball into the circle," she tells kit
zoe's ball lands inside. kit's ball drops short of the hoop
"try harder!" zoe calls. kit throws again. his ball flies past the hoop
kit lowers his arm. "i don't want to throw anymore." zoe picks up both balls
she rolls the red ball along the ground. it stops inside the hoop
"we could roll them," says zoe. kit kneels beside her and takes his blue ball
his first roll goes wide. kit fetches his ball and tries from a little closer
the blue ball stops beside zoe's red ball. "let's roll again," says kit
a small cart must reach the model library. a step stands in the way
kit pushes the cart at the step. its wheels stop against the tall edge
zoe rests a short board against the step. the board makes a ramp
kit pushes the cart up the ramp. the steep slope feels hard to climb
they keep the same step but choose a longer board. the new slope is gentler
kit tries again. this time, a smaller push moves the cart up
the cart reaches the library door. its wheels stayed on the ramp all the way
the cart cannot roll up the tall step. the gentle ramp gives it a rolling route
zoe's toy bridge is magic. "long" makes it stretch. "short" makes it shrink
kit wants to park across the blue cloth river. the bridge does not reach the other bank
"long!" zoe says. both ends now rest on the banks. kit starts the truck across
one end blocks zoe's toy garage. "short!" she calls. the bridge slides away from the far bank
the truck tilts at the edge. kit holds it still. "i haven't crossed yet!"
zoe says "long" again. the bridge reaches the bank, and kit rolls the truck off
kit parks beside the garage. zoe shortens the empty bridge and moves it away from the door
the truck fits inside the garage. kit closes the door with one finger
kit wants to find the pond in the park. he looks at the path map
a blue shape stands for the pond. a small gate picture shows the entrance
kit finds the gate beside him. he turns the map to face the same way
the map shows a path from the gate to a bench. kit follows that path
at the bench, two paths split. only one path on the map leads to the pond
kit traces that path with a finger. he takes the turn beside the tall tree
the pond comes into view. its curved edge matches the blue shape on the map
kit looks back at his route. gate, bench, tree, pond: the small map helped him find a real place
zoe watches daylight fade outside. where does the bright sunshine go
earth is round, and it spins. the sun lights the side facing it
zoe puts a dot on a ball. the dot stands for her home on earth
kit holds a flashlight still. its light falls on one side of the ball
zoe turns the ball slowly. her dot moves away from the light and into darkness
that is like night at zoe's home. other places still face the sun
she keeps turning. the dot comes back into the light, like morning
the light did not circle the ball. the turning ball changed which side was bright
a beaver carries a branch across the stream. is it building a home
it pushes the branch into a dam. mud fills some of the gaps
the dam slows the flowing water. a pond grows deeper behind it
the beaver's home is a lodge in the pond. the dam and lodge are different
an opening lies under the water. the beaver swims through it and up a short tunnel
inside, a dry room sits above the water. the beaver rests there
outside, water still trickles through the dam. the pond covers the lodge's opening
the dam holds back water. the lodge shelters the beaver. the two structures have different jobs
a dam is not a home
a dragonfly flies over the pond. its life began in the water below
a young dragonfly hatches from an egg. this wingless stage is called a nymph
the nymph hides among water plants. it catches smaller animals for food
as it grows, the nymph sheds its tight outer skin again and again
at last, it climbs up a stem and out of the water
its old skin splits. an adult dragonfly pulls free, with soft folded wings
the wings spread and harden. soon, the dragonfly can fly above the pond
a female lays eggs in a water plant. more nymphs will grow below the flying adults
a bird and a bat both fly. does that make a bat a bird
look at the bird's wing. long feathers overlap along its edge
a bat's wing has no feathers. thin skin stretches over long finger bones
soft fur covers the bat's body. the bird has feathers on its body
a mother bat feeds her baby milk. bats belong to the mammal group
birds lay eggs. baby birds hatch with beaks and grow feathers
flying tells us how an animal moves. fur and feathers tell us about its body
wings help both animals fly. the bat's fur and milk show why it belongs with mammals, not birds
an apple core is left after snack. can this scrap help something grow
kit adds it to a compost bin with dry leaves and other fruit scraps
zoe covers the scraps with more dry leaves. small living things begin breaking them down
the pile needs air and some water. a grown-up turns it and checks that it stays damp
weeks pass. the scraps get smaller and the pile sinks. it is not ready yet
after several months, the finished compost is dark and crumbly. the apple core is no longer there
kit and zoe mix some compost into garden soil. they plant a young tomato plant
the plant grows new leaves. compost from old scraps helps its soil hold water and nutrients
kit brings his orange box to the table. tomorrow he will show his class some things that matter to him
inside are a tiny sock and a blue train. "that train went everywhere with me," kit tells zoe
now kit likes making kites. he puts his newest kite on top, but the lid will not close
"too full," says zoe. kit lifts out the train. the lid shuts, but he keeps looking at the blue wheels
"i do not play with it much now," he says. "i still want to tell them about it."
zoe slides over a drawing card. kit puts the train beside it and starts with the four blue wheels
he draws the chimney, too. then he adds the long track he used to build around his bed
kit opens the box. his picture slides under the little sock. the red kite fits beside it
"old train. new kite," kit says. he closes the lid without a bump and pats the smooth orange top
the train goes back on kit's shelf. in the box, there is room for the things he wants to say
the box that would not shut
kit's blocks fall with a clatter. zoe pulls her blue chair away from the rug and keeps drawing
"come and build," kit calls. zoe holds up one finger. "i want to finish this first."
kit stacks the blocks beside her table. now she can join without moving. he adds one more block
clack! the stack tips over. zoe's pencil jerks, leaving a long green line across her picture
zoe carries her picture to the far table. kit stays by the blocks. "did you not want me here?"
"i wanted quiet," she says. kit looks at the blocks, then at the long green line
"where can i build?" he asks. zoe points to the rug. "there. i can show you when i finish."
kit carries the blocks back in two quiet loads. he makes a low bridge that does not need a tall tower
zoe adds little leaves along the stray line. it becomes another branch. then she waves kit over
kit comes with empty hands. zoe moves her picture between them. "this branch was your loud bit," she says
water pours from a tap. after washing a cup, the used water slips down the drain. where does it go
look under this sink. one pipe brings water in. a different pipe takes the used water away
in this town, water comes from a river. it travels to a treatment plant before reaching homes
at the plant, several steps remove dirt and harmful germs. workers test the water before it enters the supply pipes
those pipes carry treated water through the town. smaller pipes lead into each home, including the pipe beneath our tap
now follow the gray drain. used sink water joins other used water in a larger pipe called a sewer
the sewer leads to another treatment plant. this plant cleans used water, which may contain soap, scraps, and other waste
workers remove waste and check the treated water. in this town, it can then flow back into the river
the river does not belong to the sink. fish and plants need that water, too, so cleaning it matters
at the sink, two pipes show two different routes: treated water coming in and used water going out
zoe has a magic pocket. open it into the breeze, zip it shut, and the wind stays inside
when zoe opens the pocket again, the saved wind rushes out. kit's loose kite lifts from the grass
the kite catches in the tree's low fork. kit pulls the string, but the red paper presses against a twig
zoe catches another gust in her pocket. "i will blow it out," she says, standing beneath the kite
she opens the pocket wide. whoosh! the kite jumps higher and sticks deeper in the fork
kit stops pulling. zoe walks around the tree. from here, she can see a clear gap behind the kite
she fills the pocket once more and points it through the gap. this time she opens only a tiny corner
a little puff lifts one kite corner. kit holds out his hands as zoe lets a second puff escape
the kite slides out into kit's hands. its paper is bent, but there is no hole. zoe shuts the pocket
kit smooths the bent corner. "save some wind for flying," he says. zoe gives the zipped pocket a small pat
water surrounds most of kit's clay land. "an island?" he asks. zoe looks at the narrow strip behind it
the strip joins the large piece of land. a tiny toy can walk along it without crossing water
this shape is a peninsula. water is around most of it, but land still connects it to the mainland
zoe traces the water's edge with one finger above the tray. her finger cannot go around the land in a circle
kit lifts out the narrow strip with a flat stick. water flows into the gap between the two clay pieces
now water surrounds the smaller piece on every side. the model has an island
zoe puts the toy on the mainland. to reach the island now, it would need a boat or a bridge
real islands can sit in lakes, rivers, or oceans. their size does not change the water all around them
a real peninsula may be very wide. look for the land connection, not just the shape of its tip
back at the tray, zoe replaces the clay strip. the island becomes a peninsula again. the dry path makes the difference
look closely at the moon. many round hollows mark its surface. what punched those holes
a rock races through space toward the moon. the moon has very little air to slow it down
the rock hits hard. the crash digs into the ground and throws broken rock out around the hole
the hole is an impact crater. a raised edge, called a rim, often circles the hollow
some craters are small. others are much wider than a city. not every crash leaves the same-sized mark
on earth, rain and flowing water can wear old marks away. wind and other changes help reshape the ground
the moon has no rain or flowing rivers. many crater marks remain for a very long time
new impacts can change old marks. here, a smaller crater cuts across the rim of a larger one
that broken edge is a clue. the large crater was already there when the smaller one struck its rim
the moon's hollows are more than spots. they hold clues about crashes that changed the surface, one impact after another
a fly moves through the garden. nearby, an orb-weaving spider waits in a web shaped like a wheel
the spider made the web from silk. strong lines attach it to the stems on either side
other lines reach from the edges to the middle. these spokes help hold the web in place
between the spokes, a sticky silk line curls around the center. this part can hold a small insect
the fly hits that sticky line. its legs and wings struggle, making the silk move
the spider feels the moving threads through its legs. it turns toward the place where the fly is caught
the spider follows the threads. its feet touch only small parts of the web, and not every line is sticky
it wraps the fly in more silk. the captured insect will be food for the spider
the fly's struggle broke part of the spiral. a small gap remains where the insect was caught
the spider waits again. its silk web can catch food and carry tiny movements to its feet
this dry bean is a seed. inside its coat is a tiny plant waiting for the right conditions
in warm, damp soil, the seed takes in water. it swells, and its coat begins to split
a small root grows out first. it reaches into the soil, taking in water as the new plant grows
a shoot rises toward the light. the thick seed halves feed the young plant while its first leaves open
the leaves use sunlight to help the plant make food. more roots, stems, and leaves grow
later, small flowers open among the leaves. each flower has parts that can help form seeds
after a flower is pollinated, a pod can grow. the new seeds develop inside it
the pod grows longer. look closely: the beans inside make small bumps along its sides
left on the plant, this pod dries and turns brown. its firm beans are ready to be collected as seeds
one of those beans goes into warm, damp soil. a new root begins the journey again
kit puts a shiny paper clip beside shiny foil. "will the magnet pull both?" zoe brings two empty trays
the magnet pulls the steel clip. kit lifts the magnet, and the clip hangs from one end
zoe tries the foil. it stays on the table, even when the same end of the magnet comes close
both objects are metal, but only the steel clip moved. being shiny was not enough to tell them apart
a wooden block stays still, too. kit puts it in the tray with the foil
the plastic spoon does not move toward the magnet. zoe adds it to the same tray
now kit tries a steel washer. the magnet lifts it, just as it lifted the clip
steel usually contains plenty of iron. magnets attract iron, but they do not pull every kind of metal like this
the children put a steel key beside the trays. before sorting it, they test it with the magnet
the key lifts. into the clip tray it goes. these groups tell what the magnet did, not what looked shiny
the garden light shines after sunset. its small solar panel is dark. what keeps the lamp glowing
earlier, sunlight fell on the panel. the panel changed some of that light energy into electricity
inside the light, wires carry electricity to a battery. the battery stores energy for later
the sun moves across the sky while the battery charges. the lamp does not need to shine in daylight
as evening grows dark, a control switches the lamp on. the battery now supplies energy to the light
that is why the lamp can glow without sunlight. energy collected earlier is being used now
but the battery cannot store an endless supply. if little sunlight reaches the panel, the light may not last as long
a leaf covers part of this panel during the day. removing it lets more sunlight reach the panel again
the light uses energy from the sun, but its parts still need materials and care. using less light saves energy, too
daytime light, stored energy, nighttime lamp: the battery connects two parts of the day. the garden path is bright enough to see
"kit can build our stage," zoe says. kit reaches for the cardboard, but his eyes stay on the orange fox puppet
he makes a wide window and hangs the blue curtain. everyone will see the puppets through the opening he has made
while zoe practices the rabbit's lines, kit speaks softly behind the stage. "who has been digging near my den?"
zoe leans around the curtain. "that voice is good! make one surprised noise when i knock on the door."
kit tries the voice on her signal. then he stops. there is more he wants to say than one surprised noise
"i want to play the fox," he says. zoe looks at the stage. "but you are our builder."
"i built it already," kit says. he slips his hand into the puppet. "can i try the whole part?"
they begin again. kit forgets one line, so zoe taps the little den on the scenery. he finds the words
at the show, the fox peeps out. kit's voice reaches the back row. "who has been digging near my den?"
zoe's rabbit raises one muddy paw. behind the curtain, kit nearly laughs. the stage holds up, and so does his fox voice
zoe draws the lost red ball beside the dog's bed. kit turns the page. "that is where our story stops?"
"the dog found it," zoe says. but kit is already sketching a new page: the dog sits on the ball by mistake
he slips his page over hers. "now it is funny." zoe pulls the book toward her and presses it shut
later, kit opens the book. his new page is gone. zoe's dog curls beside the ball as if nothing happened
"you took mine out." "you covered mine first." the dog has its ball, but neither child wants to turn the page
zoe smooths her page. "he looked for it all day. i wanted him to have a rest." kit studies the tired dog
"i wanted one last laugh," kit says. he holds his page beside hers. zoe points at the round ball under the dog
they move the ball into the bed on the first page. on the next, the sleepy dog sits down without looking
the dog pops up. the ball rolls out. then the dog curls down, with the ball safely beside the bed
kit turns the last page slowly. zoe nudges him when the dog jumps. they keep both the laugh and the rest
rain taps the roof and runs along the path. before long, water is rushing toward the stream behind the community building
the roof and pavement let little water soak through. water flowing over the surface is called runoff
as runoff travels, it can pick up loose dirt and litter. those things may reach the stream with the water
this community gives some of the rain another route. a downspout directs roof water toward a shallow planted hollow
the hollow is a rain garden. it holds water briefly while the water slowly passes into the soil below
plants and soil slow the flow and help trap some of the dirt. roots take up water as the plants grow
the garden must suit its place. workers check the soil and plan a safe route for water that cannot soak in
during very heavy rain, extra water can leave through that overflow route. a rain garden cannot hold every storm
after the shower, the pooled water sinks away. flowers remain beside the path, and less roof water has rushed straight downstream
the garden changes the journey of the rain: pause, spread, soak. a patch of planted ground becomes part of the town's drainage
zoe's silver chalk makes a door in any wall. the whole outline must join, or the wall stays solid
today, their round paper moon will not fit through the ordinary doorway. kit holds it while zoe reaches for the chalk
she wipes away the small door and draws a tall, narrow rectangle. when the last line joins, the puppet room appears
kit tilts the moon, but it still catches. one side dents. "taller did not make it wider," he says
zoe rests the moon on the floor. she stretches string across it, then carries that width to the wall
she wipes away one side and draws it farther out. as the outline closes, the wider doorway opens
kit carries the moon through. his sleeve brushes the chalk. a gap appears, and the doorway closes behind him
"zoe?" kit calls from the other room. she follows the pale line with her finger until she finds the missing piece
one short chalk stroke joins the gap. kit appears with the moon still in his hands. "i was waiting right here."
they hang the moon above the curtain. after both return, zoe wipes the outline away. this time, she means to close it
this river bend has two very different edges. one bank is steep. across the water, a low strip of sand slopes gently
moving water can loosen soil and carry it away. that wearing away is called erosion. watch the outside of the bend
here, faster water presses against the bank. bits of soil fall into the flow, leaving the edge farther back
the river carries this loose material, called sediment. fine grains travel in the water; heavier pieces may roll below
where the current slows, it cannot keep carrying the same load. some sediment settles onto the riverbed
leaving sediment behind is called deposition. on the inside of this bend, sand collects into a shallow bar
over time, the outside edge wears back while the inside bar grows. the curve of the river slowly shifts
a heavy flow can move larger pieces than a gentle flow. after a storm, the bank and bar may change more quickly
when the water drops, fresh sand remains. the river has not simply taken land away; it has left material in new places
look again at the steep bank and sandy bar. one bend shows two connected changes: ground removed here and sediment left there
one evening, the moon looks like a thin curved slice. later, it looks round and bright. has part of it disappeared
the moon is still a whole round world. sunlight lights the half facing the sun, while the other half is dark
but we watch from earth, not from the sun. we do not always see the entire sunlit half
as the moon travels around earth, our view changes. different amounts of the bright half face toward us
near new moon, the sunlit half mostly faces away from earth. the moon is usually hard to see in the bright sky
a few days later, a bright crescent appears. we can see only a narrow part of the moon's sunlit half
about a week after new moon, half the moon's face looks bright. the whole moon has not changed shape
near full moon, earth faces almost all of the sunlit half. the bright disk looks round again
after that, the bright part we see gets smaller. the pattern repeats in about a month as the moon keeps orbiting
these changing views are called phases. earth's shadow makes a lunar eclipse, a different event. ordinary phases come from our changing viewpoint
when the desert grows dark, a saguaro flower opens. a bat is coming for a meal, but not to catch an insect
this lesser long-nosed bat drinks nectar, the sweet liquid inside flowers. its long muzzle fits into the open bloom
a long tongue reaches deeper than its nose. as the bat feeds, dusty pollen sticks to the fur around its face
the flower has given the bat food. what happens to the pollen when the bat flies away
the bat visits a flower on another saguaro. some pollen rubs onto the sticky part in the middle of that flower
that transfer is pollination. it can help the flower make seeds. the bat carries pollen without trying to grow a plant
after pollination and other changes inside the flower, a fruit may develop. its seeds will hold the next generation of saguaros
later still, the ripe fruit opens. dark seeds sit inside the red flesh, far above the desert ground
birds and insects can pollinate saguaro flowers, too. the bat is one visitor in a larger web of living things
return to the night flower. nectar feeds the bat; carried pollen helps the cactus make seeds. one meal connects two lives
a small frog sits at the pond's edge. months earlier, it could not hop here. it swam underwater with a tail
its life began inside an egg. common frog eggs lie in soft clumps of jelly near the water's surface
a tadpole hatched from an egg. it swam by moving its tail and used gills to take oxygen from the water
as it grew, its back legs appeared first. for a while, it had both a swimming tail and little legs
front legs appeared, too. inside, its body was changing: lungs developed while its gills became less important
the tail did not fall off. the body absorbed it, using its materials as the young frog continued to change
now the froglet could climb onto a damp bank. its new legs, lungs, and changing body helped it use another place
adult common frogs breathe with lungs and moist skin. they can hunt small animals on land, but they still need damp places
when breeding time comes, adults return to water. new eggs begin another generation, not the same frog's life all over again
egg, tadpole, froglet, adult: the changes fit different ways of living. a tiny swimmer becomes a frog at the water's edge
a frog changes its way of life
a whale swims past a school of fish. both have streamlined bodies for swimming. why are they placed in different groups
living in the same place does not make animals the same kind. their bodies and life histories give us more clues
watch the whale rise. it takes air into lungs through blowholes on top of its head, then dives while holding its breath
the fish stay below. their gills take oxygen from water passing over them. they do not need the whale's surface-breathing routine
the whale's calf was born alive and drinks milk made by its mother. feeding young with milk is a mammal trait
whales also keep their bodies warm from within. a thick layer of fat helps hold that warmth in the cold sea
some sharks give birth to live young, too. sharks are fish. that one clue alone cannot tell us "mammal."
scientists use several clues, including body features and how animals are related. whales belong with mammals despite their fishlike outline
dolphins are mammals, too. like whales, they breathe air and feed their young milk, although they spend their lives in water
the ocean tells us where these animals live. their connected features tell us more about the groups they belong to
a whale is not a fish
the garden soil looks pale and dry on top. kit lifts the watering can, but zoe kneels beside a plant first
the gardener helps them check below the surface. the soil underneath is darker and still damp. the top did not tell everything
plant roots take up water from the soil. water left on a hot path cannot help these roots in the same way
some soil water escapes into the air as invisible vapor. this change is evaporation, and sun and wind can speed it up
the gardener spreads clean straw over the bare soil. this covering is mulch. it slows water loss and shades the ground
zoe leaves space around each stem. mulch should cover the soil, not pile up against the plants. they check beneath it later
another morning, the soil near the roots is becoming dry. kit waters slowly beside the plants, keeping water off the path
a little at a time lets water soak in. if water runs away, pouring faster will not put more around the roots
the next morning, they lift the straw and check again. the soil is damp, so the watering can stays by the gate
leaves stand above the covering of straw. the children have saved water by keeping it useful, without leaving the plants thirsty
keep the water in the garden
kit and zoe walk to play
he waits and waves to zoe
the huge wheel does not fit
the shell stays on wet sand
a space rock enters earth's air
this crab needs a bigger shell
the old shell is too small
it finds a small empty shell
that shell is too small too
here is a bigger empty shell
it moves into the bigger shell
its soft wings cannot lift it
the butterfly flies to a flower
the crackers wait for snack time
kit wants a long road for his truck
he carries more blocks. his arms feel tired
kit picks up another block. it slips onto the rug
"i need a break," says kit. he sits down
zoe adds one block. kit watches from his seat
kit rests a little longer. the last gap stays open
kit gets up. "i want to put that one in."
he fills the gap. his truck rolls all the way
zoe saves a cracker for her cheese. she gets a cup
kit sees the cracker. he eats it
zoe comes back. "my cheese has no cracker now."
kit offers a crumb. zoe shakes her head
kit opens his box. one whole cracker is still inside
"would you like mine?" asks kit. "yes," says zoe
kit puts his cracker on her plate
zoe puts the cheese on top. this bite has a cracker
kit puts a picture in an envelope. he writes zoe's address
he seals the flap. the letter goes into the mailbox
a worker collects the mail. kit's letter joins the other letters
a machine reads the address. the letters go into groups
a van carries this group to zoe's area
here is zoe's street. the carrier checks each address
the carrier puts the letter through zoe's door
zoe opens it. kit's small picture has come a long way
the magic clips swap colors. a red cup. a blue cart
kit clips both. his cart turns red. her cup turns blue
zoe reaches for her cup. "that is not my red cup!"
kit swaps them back. zoe takes her red cup
kit still wants a red cart. he finds red paper
"may i use this?" zoe slides the paper over
kit clips the blue cart and red paper. their colors swap
kit rolls his red cart. zoe's red cup stays red
sea water covers a dip in rock
slowly, the sea falls. the rock begins to show
more rock shows. water stays in the deep dip
the sea is lower now. the pool is still here
rock holds the water around the sides
the sea starts to rise again
water spills over the rim. the pool joins the sea
sea in, sea out. the rock dip keeps a pool
this robot rolls across mars. it has six wheels
rocks lie ahead. there is no smooth road
the front wheel climbs the small rock
the wheel supports bend at their joints
now the middle wheel rolls over the rock
the back wheel follows. the front wheel dips down
the wheels come back onto level ground
the wheels rise and fall. joints help the rover cross rough ground
is that a twig on the stem
look again. six legs grip the plant
a stick insect hides among twigs
its long brown body looks like a twig
still legs are hard to spot among twigs
one leg lifts. the insect takes a slow step
it reaches a leaf and takes a bite
its shape helps it hide. its moving legs help us find it
grasshopper eggs lie in the soil
a small hopper comes out. it has no long wings
it eats leaves. its body grows
its tight outer skin splits. the grasshopper pulls free
it grows and sheds its skin again. small wing pads grow
after the last shed, long wings open and become firm
now the grown grasshopper can fly
the little hopper grows wings in stages. now it can hop and fly
can light get through these three sheets
kit shines a flashlight through clear plastic. the wall stays bright
zoe holds up wax paper. a soft glow shows through
now she holds thick card. a dark patch covers the wall
zoe puts the card in one group. it blocks the light
the plastic and wax paper go together. both let light through
kit looks through both. one gives a clear view. one blurs it
two groups become three. clear view, blurred view, no view
zoe turns the faucet off. a drop still falls
kit tries the handle. drip. it still leaks
zoe puts a cup below it. drip, drip, drip
the cup is half full. zoe shows the leak to a grown-up
the grown-up shuts off the water. she fits a new part
she turns the water back on. kit tests the faucet
he closes it. they wait. no drops fall
zoe waters a plant with the saved water. the cup stays empty
kit wants a picnic under the tree. he will bring the mat, two cups, and their red ball
zoe draws the three things. kit studies her picture, leaves it on the table, and goes inside
he brings the cups and ball. zoe points at the grass. "what will we sit on?"
kit shuts his eyes to picture the card. he opens them again. "i keep losing one bit."
he taps three fingers. "mat, cups, ball." then he says it again, with a little beat
"mat, cups, ball." kit points to the cups and ball. "the mat!" he runs back to the shelf
he carries the mat outside and spreads it flat. "mat, cups, ball," he says, checking each one
zoe sits at one end. kit puts down the cups, then rolls the ball to her. nothing is missing
kit folds the paper around their parcel. "where is the ribbon?" zoe points across the room. "by the pot."
kit looks beside the tall blue pot at the window. there is a watering can, but no ribbon
"i cannot find it," he calls. zoe raises her voice. "it is by the pot!"
kit looks under the blue pot's tray. still no ribbon. he puts the tray back and stops searching
"which pot?" he asks. zoe looks at the window, then points to the shelf. "the small yellow one."
"the yellow pot on the shelf?" "yes." kit walks past the window and reaches beside the little pot
his hand closes around the red ribbon. he carries it to zoe, keeping the long end off the floor
zoe holds the knot while kit pulls the bow. their parcel stays shut, with two red loops on top
before the market opens, one table stands empty. what must happen before carrots can fill it
at a nearby farm, a grower pulls carrots from the soil. she gathers them in a green crate
the full crate goes into her van. she takes the carrots to the market with the other growers
the worker holds the gate open and points out a space. the grower carries the crate to her table
the grower lifts carrots onto the stand. she keeps the empty crate underneath for the trip home
kit arrives with a grown-up. he points to a bunch of carrots and asks the grower about them
the grown-up pays. the grower passes the carrots across, and kit puts them in their cloth bag
the table was empty before the growers came. growing, carrying, and setting out the food made this market ready
zoe's red bookmark is magic. it slides along pencil arrows, but blank paper makes it stop
kit wants it to find his page by itself. he draws an arrow path across a long strip of paper
the bookmark turns back at one arrow. then it slides forward again, still far from kit's page
kit picks it up and starts again. the bookmark reaches that patch and turns back, just as before
"let's follow the points," zoe says. kit traces the arrows. one point sends his finger the wrong way
he rubs out that arrow and draws it toward the book. the paper now gives one clear route
the bookmark slides past the repaired place and onto kit's page. this time, it does not come back
zoe pulls the arrow strip away. kit closes the book. a red tip waits exactly where his reading stopped
dark rock covers this old lava flow. it once moved. how did flowing lava become solid ground
during an eruption, hot melted rock reaches the surface. we call it lava
the lava spreads over the ground. its outside loses heat to the cooler air and ground
a thin solid crust forms outside. under that dark crust, hotter lava can still flow
here, the crust cracks. bright lava shows through the gap. a dark top does not mean a cool inside
as more heat escapes, the solid layer grows thicker. the hot middle cools more slowly
much later, the whole flow becomes solid rock. thick flows can take years to reach this stage
the rock keeps the shape of the old flow. melted rock spread here, then cooling made it solid
a comet has a long pale tail. is that tail part of a solid body
far from the sun, the comet is a small frozen body with dust trapped in its ice
nearer the sun, the ice warms. gas escapes and carries some of the dust away
the loose dust spreads away from the small center. it is no longer trapped in solid ice
the dust reflects sunlight. we see a pale tail, even though the dust pieces are tiny
the solid center is much smaller than the tail. most of that long shape is scattered dust
farther from the sun, less dust escapes. the visible tail grows faint as the comet moves away
the long tail is not a solid piece of the comet. it is loose dust, lit by the sun
a sea otter finds a clam on the seabed. food lies inside, behind a hard shell
the otter takes the clam and a flat stone. it swims back up through the kelp
at the surface, it rolls onto its back. the clam rests on its chest above the water
the otter sets the stone on its chest. it holds the clam above the flat surface
tap! the clam hits the stone, but its shell stays closed
the otter strikes again. a crack opens in the hard shell
its paws pull the broken shell apart. now it can reach the food inside
the stone stays outside the otter's body, but it helps the otter get food. the stone is a tool
small round eggs lie in a hole in the soil. a garden snail laid them here
inside each egg, a young snail grows. these eggs are darker now, close to hatching
a tiny snail pushes out. it already carries a small shell on its back
the young snail eats soft leaves. its body grows, and its shell grows with it
it does not leave that shell to find a larger one. the shell remains part of its growing body
many months pass. the snail becomes much larger, with a broad, patterned shell
when this snail is grown and has mated, it can lay eggs in another soil hole
a new snail begins in an egg with its own shell. one body and its shell grow together
salt and sand both look like tiny grains. kit puts a small scoop of each beside two cups of water
zoe tips salt into the first cup and stirs. the white grains become harder to see
soon, the water looks clear. "has the salt gone?" kit asks. they leave that cup on its blue mat
kit stirs sand into the other cup. grains swirl, then sink into a layer when he stops
zoe pours a little clear salt water into a dish. they leave it by the window for several days
the water slowly dries away. small white salt crystals appear on the dish. the salt was still there
salt can spread through water without visible grains. sand stays in grains, even after stirring
both began as grains. the water test puts them in different groups: dissolves and does not dissolve
this fallen log lies beside the path. kit lifts one end to clear the ground
underneath, the soil is dark and damp. tiny gray woodlice hurry into the shade
woodlice lose water easily. cool, damp spaces help them stay moist
they feed on dead plant pieces. some are nibbling the soft wood and fallen leaves
zoe points to the busy patch. moving the log would take away its cover
kit lowers the log gently into its old place. he keeps its damp side against the soil
they move a discarded wrapper from the path instead. the log stays beside the fern
the path is clear. beneath the log, shade and damp shelter remain for the small animals living there
zoe draws her best day: purple boots splashing in a puddle. kit draws a ball beneath a bright sun
when zoe adds a rain cloud, kit looks up. "my best day had sunshine. would yours look better with a sun?"
he holds out a yellow paper sun. zoe lays it over her cloud and puts down the blue crayon
the picture is bright now, but zoe frowns. without the rain, her puddle seems like the wrong part of the day
she remembers the splash reaching her knees. that was the part she had wanted to draw
zoe lifts the paper sun. "i liked the rain," she says. "it made a puddle big enough to jump in."
"but you got wet," says kit. zoe grins. "my boots got wet. i wanted one more jump."
she draws blue rain below the cloud. now the boots, the splashes, and the sky belong in the same picture
kit holds up his sunny picture. zoe holds up her rainy one. neither asks the other to change it
they clip both pictures to the ledge. zoe points to the biggest splash. "that is why i picked this day."
zoe leaves her little house on the table while she gets tape. kit spots a hole in its roof
"i can fix that," he says. he lays a cardboard patch over the hole and presses tape along its edges
zoe comes back and bends over the roof. "now i can't see the bed!" she says
"i thought it was broken." kit pulls at the patch. a piece of the roof tears up with it
zoe catches his hand. "wait. i made that opening so we could look inside." kit lets go
he looks at the torn edge. "what do you want to keep?" zoe points around the hole. "all this space."
together they ease off the last tape. kit holds the roof still while zoe slips a strip beneath the tear
she tapes the strip in place. kit presses the bent edge flat, leaving the opening clear
"anything else?" he asks. zoe looks through the roof. "move the bed a little. it's hiding behind the wall."
kit slides the bed into view. they lean over the opening together. this time, both can see inside
at this corner, kit watches the orange hand across the street. beside him, an adult listens near the crossing button
a quiet sound helps the adult find the button. that sound does not mean it is time to cross
the adult presses the button. a raised arrow on its surface points along the crossing they want to use
kit can see the arrow. the adult can feel its shape without needing to see the mark
they wait. pressing the button does not make the cars stop at once
now the white walking figure appears. a faster ticking sound comes from the button beside them
the arrow vibrates too. the adult feels it under a fingertip while kit watches the walking figure
the light, sound, and movement give the walk message in different ways. they do not move the traffic themselves
the adult checks the traffic before they cross together. kit stays beside the tapping cane
on the far sidewalk, kit looks back. that little box had more than one way to say the same thing
zoe draws a silver circle. "stand here," she says. "it lends you a giant shadow that copies your shape."
kit steps inside. a huge shadow rises on the wall, though there is no lamp behind him
he lifts one hand. the shadow lifts one hand. he spreads his fingers, and its huge fingers spread too
"wave the fan!" zoe says. the little red fan rests on a chair beside the shadow's hand
kit closes his fingers around the air. on the wall, the shadow's fist passes right through the fan
he tries again, more slowly. the fan stays still. "your hand is flat," zoe tells the shadow
kit looks at his own empty fingers. "it's copying me," he says. "i need something to hold."
zoe brings him the real fan. when kit holds it up, a dark fan grows above the giant hand
kit sweeps his arm. the tiny red fan waves, and its enormous shadow sails across the wall
zoe waves back with both hands. kit bows, and a giant bow carries the shadow fan almost to the floor
this sandy hill is a dune. beside a dark rock, its steep edge seems to stand still
look closer on a windy day. loose grains roll and hop along the ground
when one hopping grain lands, it can knock other grains loose. soon more sand is moving
the wind carries sand up the dune's gentle side. grain after grain reaches the top
sand gathers beyond the top. when too much piles there, some slips down the steep side
the sliding sand settles at the bottom. the steep edge now reaches a little farther forward
meanwhile, wind keeps taking grains from the other side. the hill changes as sand leaves one place and fills another
after many windy days, compare the dune with the rock. its steep edge is farther away than before
the rock did not walk, and the dune did not jump. thousands of small movements changed the hill's position
a hill can travel one grain at a time. here, the wind keeps moving sand toward the dune's steep side
the full moon rises bright and round. later, a dark curved edge begins to cover its face
the moon shines because sunlight reaches it and reflects toward earth. what could block that sunlight
tonight, earth is between the sun and moon. our planet casts a long shadow behind it
as the moon moves into that shadow, less direct sunlight reaches its surface. the dark patch spreads
soon the whole moon is inside the darkest part. it may look rusty red instead of disappearing
some sunlight passes through the air around earth. this filtered light can still reach the moon
the moon keeps moving. after a while, a bright edge appears as it begins to leave the shadow
more of its face returns to sunlight. at last, the round moon shines brightly again
this change happens over hours. the moon's usual phases change across many nights as it travels around earth
nothing took a bite out of the moon. earth briefly stood in the way of its sunlight
a butterfly rests beside a green leaf. part of its wing seems to be missing. can you see the leaf through it
this is a glasswing butterfly. the clear patch is a real part of its wing, not an empty hole
light passes through that thin surface. light from the green leaf can still reach our eyes
follow the dark lines across the clear patch. these veins help support the wing
the brown border is easier to see. it has many tiny scales, packed more closely than in the clear area
now the butterfly lands beside a pale flower. look at the same clear patch against this new background
the patch looks pale instead of green. the wing has not turned into a flower; we are seeing what lies behind it
its dark body and wing edges still stand out. clear wings do not make the whole butterfly disappear
when the wings lift, their thin surfaces move together. each clear patch belongs to a complete wing
look back at the leaf. what seemed missing was there all along: a wing that lets much of the light through
a young blue crab grows inside a hard covering. that covering protects it, but it cannot stretch enough as the crab grows
under the old covering, a new one begins to form. for now, the new covering is soft
soon the old shell opens along the back. the crab starts pulling its body away from the hard outer layer
it backs out, drawing its legs and claws free. the old covering stays behind on the estuary floor
now two crab shapes lie beside the stone. one is a living crab. the other is an empty covering
the soft crab takes in water, which helps its new covering expand. there is more room for its growing body
while the covering is soft, the crab is easier to hurt. it stays sheltered among the grass
its new covering hardens. the soft stage does not last for the rest of the crab's life
the crab moves out to find food. as this young crab keeps growing, it will need to shed again
the empty shape cannot follow. a crab did not become two crabs; one crab left its old covering behind
a crab leaves its old coat
a red tomato and a green pea pod sit on the table. which one is a fruit
open the tomato and look inside. small seeds sit in soft, wet pockets beneath the skin
the tomato grew from a flower. as the fruit developed, its seeds grew inside it
now look inside the pea pod. six round peas lie in a row. each pea is a seed
the pod grew from a flower too. it is the fruit around those seeds, though it looks unlike the tomato
a pea and its pod have different jobs. the seed holds a tiny new plant; the pod surrounds the seeds
the whole pod is not one giant seed. its long wall holds several separate seeds together
the tomato has seeds too, but they are smaller and surrounded by soft flesh. fruits need not look alike
point to a seed in each dish. then point to the fruit that grew around those seeds
both dishes hold fruit and seeds. the pod belongs with the tomato, even though its seeds look very different
this porch lamp helps people see the path. but its bare bulb also sends light toward the window and hedge
from the gate, the bright bulb is easy to spot. the darker path below is harder to see beside its glare
does the light need to reach every place? the path needs light. the upstairs window does not
the adult turns the power off before fitting a shield above the bulb. zoe watches from the doorway
when the lamp comes on again, the shield blocks light from shining straight upward
more of the useful light falls onto the path. the hedge and window no longer catch the same bright spill
a lamp can also be brighter than a place needs. this path needs enough light to show its edges
light sent into the sky can make stars harder to see. a shield helps keep this lamp's light closer to home
later, when nobody needs the path, the timer turns the lamp off. the porch grows dark again
the lamp is ready for the next visitor. for now, the path, hedge, and window share the night
zoe draws the day she learned to blow bubbles in the pool. at first, she had been afraid of the water
now she wants everyone to see the bubbles, but she does not want to show the worried picture beside them
she folds the worried half behind the happy half. kit reaches for the clip. "we can hang it here."
as she lifts the drawing, the folded half swings open. zoe pulls it back before kit can hang it
"maybe i should keep it all," she says. she lowers the sheet, though her finger still rests on the bubbles
kit puts down his hand. "which part do you want us to see?" zoe points to the swimmer in the water
"this part. the other part is for me." she takes a fresh sheet and draws the bubbles again
the new swimmer has a wide smile. this time, there is no other picture waiting to unfold behind it
zoe slips the first drawing into her folder. then she holds out the new one for kit to hang
when kit clips it up, zoe shows him the bubbles. her first drawing is still hers, safely inside the folder
only one piece is missing from the boat. kit holds it behind his back, waiting for zoe to notice the gap
while she checks the box, he slips the piece behind the blue cushion. he plans to surprise her in a moment
zoe pulls the cushion onto her lap. a small tap sounds behind the bench, but kit is looking at her face
he checks the bench. nothing. instead of explaining, he looks in the box again, although he knows it is empty
zoe searches under the table. kit watches her crawl past the bench. the joke no longer feels like a joke
"i hid it," he says. "behind the cushion. then i lost it." zoe sits back. "why didn't you tell me?"
"i wanted a surprise. i'm sorry." kit moves beside the bench. "it made a sound when you lifted the cushion."
they look behind the bench together. a white corner lies against the wall, just beyond kit's fingers
kit reaches from the other side and lifts out the piece. he gives it to zoe instead of hiding it again
zoe fits the sail into the gap. kit waits while she presses it flat. this surprise is over; the boat is whole
at lunchtime, the courtyard bench stands in the sun. kit and zoe want a cooler place where their class can sit
a young tree grows nearby, but its small patch of shade cannot cover the bench yet
the caretaker asks them to help choose a place for shade. they draw the doorway, the bench, and the tree
next morning, a long shadow lies beside the wall. kit points to it. "could we move the bench there?"
when they return at lunchtime, that shadow has shrunk. the space kit chose is sunny when the class needs to sit
they mark a new place on their plan. it must fit the bench without blocking the way through the doorway
the caretaker takes their plan to the school. later, workers put up a shade cover beside the young tree
at lunchtime, the bench now stands beneath the cover. the children check where its shade falls before sitting down
the tree will need time to grow a wider crown. the cover gives shade while the school cares for it
their plan has room for sitting and room for passing through. it works at the time the class needs it
kit's paint hides things when dry. he wipes a hidden corner clean with a wet cloth. yellow shows again
he wants zoe to see his boat disappear. he paints its blue hull, red sail, and little mast
the yellow tray looks too plain beside it. kit paints that too, spreading purple right up to the rim
when zoe arrives, the paint is dry. the boat has vanished from sight, and so has the tray beneath it
kit reaches for the boat, but his hand brushes its sail. something bumps against a rim he cannot see
he stops reaching. if he guesses again, the boat might slide farther. zoe points to the damp cloth beside the cup
kit remembers the yellow corner he wiped. he wets the cloth and gently draws it across the hidden tray
a yellow edge appears. he follows it until the cloth touches something higher. a strip of blue shows through
now he can hold the boat still while he wipes it clean. zoe steadies the tray by its visible edge
when the tray is clean too, kit sets the boat inside. "my surprise took a little finding," he says
a small river winds through this mountain valley. the valley is so wide that the river leaves most of its floor untouched
what shaped all that space? long ago, thick ice filled much of the valley, from its floor high up its sides
this mass of ice was a glacier. although it looked still, it slowly flowed down the valley
rock caught in the bottom of the moving ice scraped against the valley floor. it left scratches in the hard stone
the moving ice also wore at the valley's sides. over a long time, the valley became wider and deeper
later, more ice melted at the glacier's front than arrived from higher up. the end of the glacier grew shorter
as the ice shrank back, it uncovered the broad valley it had helped shape. a river could flow along the bottom
today, the ice is gone from this valley. its steep sides curve into a wide floor, like the bottom of a u
on bare rock, long scratches give another clue. stones carried by the old glacier once scraped along these lines
the river still changes the valley, but it did not make this wide space alone. the missing ice left its work behind
three bright stars seem close together in the sky. from earth, we see a pattern, but we cannot see its depth
some stars in a pattern are much farther away than others. kit and zoe make a small model to explore that idea
zoe sets one model star near kit, one farther back, and one near the far end of the table
from his end, kit sees all three in a row. their places look connected, although the spaces between them are different
zoe walks to the side. from here, she can see how far the stars stretch along the table
kit joins her. the same three stars look much farther apart. they were never fixed to one flat picture
real stars are vastly farther away than these cards. walking across our yard does not give us this side view of them
we would need a view from far across space to see the pattern from a very different angle
people join star patterns in their minds to make constellations. the lines help us find shapes; they are not strings in space
the stars can share a pattern without sharing one small place. what looks close depends on where we are looking from
the mud looks almost empty, but small animals live on it and inside it. two shorebirds have come to find a meal
this plover takes a few quick steps, then stops. its short, strong bill stays above the mud while it looks
a tiny crab moves nearby. the plover darts forward and picks it from the surface before it reaches a hole
the other bird is a dowitcher. its bill is much longer than the plover's, and it searches in a wetter patch
it pushes its bill into the soft mud, lifts it, and probes again. much of its searching happens out of sight
below the surface, its bill can reach buried food. a worm does not have to come into view first
the plover often searches by watching. the dowitcher often probes. their different actions help them find food in the same place
but these are not two fixed menus. a plover can pull out a worm, and a dowitcher can pick up surface food
even when a worm stays hidden, the dowitcher's probing marks show where its bill has been
a long bill is useful for reaching in. a sharp look can help at the surface. this muddy place holds both opportunities
each autumn, monarch butterflies from eastern north america fly south. many reach mountain forests in mexico, where they spend the winter
they gather on fir trees, wings folded close. these travelers will wait through winter before beginning the journey north
when spring brings warmer days, the butterflies leave the forest. they fly north, stopping to feed as they go
along the way, females lay eggs on milkweed. the butterflies that began this trip will not travel the whole route north
their young grow into new butterflies. these are the next generation: the children of the butterflies that left the winter forest
some of these new butterflies keep moving north and lay eggs. later generations continue as milkweed grows in more northern places
by late summer, many earlier travelers are gone. their descendants feed in meadows far from the winter forest
then a new generation begins the long flight south. these butterflies have never visited the forest they are heading toward
they gather in mexico as the earlier travelers did. the route has come around again, but the butterflies have changed
no single butterfly made the whole yearly journey. like a relay, the journey continued while one generation gave way to the next
kit sorts four shapes by color. the red ones sit together, and the blue ones make a second group
zoe wants to find the round shapes together too. but each color group holds one round shape and one square
they sort by shape instead. now the circles are together, but the red pieces have become separated again
can one board show both things? they draw four spaces, with red above not red and round beside not round
the red circle belongs in the top left space. it is red, and it is round: both answers fit
the red square goes beside it. it matches the red row, but it does not belong in the round column
the blue circle fits below the red circle. the blue square fits beside it: neither red nor round, but still sorted
zoe brings a small red circle and a red triangle. their sizes and shapes differ, but the same two questions still work
the small circle joins the large one. the triangle joins the red square, because neither of those red shapes is round
sharing a space does not mean every piece is the same. it means they give the same answers to these two questions
beside the school path, tall stems carry tight green buds. the gardener has come to cut the grass around them
if the whole patch is cut now, those buds will go with the stems. they will not open into flowers there
zoe points to the buds. the gardener leaves this patch standing and cuts a route beside it, where people need to walk
weeks later, yellow flowers open above the grass. a small bee lands on a dark center and begins to feed
the short route lets kit and zoe come close without pushing through the flowers. they watch from its edge
after flowering, some petals fall. the dark heads remain, and seeds develop where the tiny flowers in each center had been
the patch looks less bright now. cutting every stem would remove these seed heads before many seeds could fall
the gardener lets this part finish making seeds. some ripe seeds drop into the spaces beneath the old stems
the path still needs care, and the patch does too. the gardener checks what is growing before planning the next cut
one place can hold a clear way through and a patch left to grow. keeping both takes more than cutting everything alike
